blocked_on: C's host lanes commit-held-host and reconfig-host merging with host calls to the subjects
detail: The ruling-19 phase models are proved, but their subjects have no host caller on dev (train 28 statement audit, build/coordinator/audits/train28-statement-audit.txt, finding 1). host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked is still inline, and host/native/owner.lisp calls fn-otm-next, not fn-otm-hold-next. Until the host lanes land, these are MODEL claims, and nothing cites them as host claims: books/owner-reconfig-phased.lisp R0-R6 (subject fn-orp-step), books/owner-time-reconfig.lisp H1, H3, H4 (fn-otm-hold-begin, fn-otm-hold-next, fn-otm-hold-end), and books/owner-time-held.lisp fn-otm-held-quantum-2-answers-the-held-outcome (fn-otm-held-event, fn-och-caller-answer, which C's lane/commit-held-host calls and dev does not yet). books/owner-reconfig-lock.lisp L1-L3 are host-reached already (fn-ocfg-step), per the audit.
fix: Land C's lane/commit-held-host and lane/reconfig-host, whose host code calls fn-otm-held-event/fn-och-caller-answer and fn-orp-step/fn-otm-hold-* respectively. Then reach_check names the subjects as reached, the keystones become host claims, and their PRF rows may be written. Teeth (defteeth) for the same statements land in lane p-ruling19-teeth.
notes: 2026-10-08 P5: PARKED (deferred). Un-parks when C's commit-held-host and reconfig-host merge to dev; P then checks reach_check on the subjects and writes the PRF rows.

2026-10-08 Codex, reconfig-host round 3: H3 integration owner deputy-C / lane commit-held-host. fnn-owner-gate-pick calls fn-otm-hold-next, whose H1 only restricts admitted classes and preserves the hold. The live committer in this tree still calls fn-otm-commit-event and fn-otm-committer-wake, not fn-otm-held-event / fn-otm-held-committer-wake, and has no may-start check. Do not infer START/collect exclusion from hold-next or claim composition safety until commit-held-host lands and C runs the combined native owner_scheduler/owner_offlock/live_reconfiguration witnesses. The reconfiguration wrapper now documents this dependency explicitly.
scenario: A reader of the ledger takes the phased reconfiguration or the held commit as running on the host while the host still runs the inline path that holds O across durable I/O.
title: Ruling 19's phase-model keystones are model claims until C's host lanes call their subjects
